comparisons.peer_summary: Quarterly net revenue and segment mix vary due to end-market demand fluctuations and seasonality. Semiconductor revenue recognition upon delivery to distributors also causes significant quarterly fluctuations, subject to estimates for returns and allowances.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom disclose that seasonality is a key driver of quarterly revenue fluctuations. Intel notes its revenue historically peaks in the fourth quarter and was consistent with this trend in 2024, whereas Broadcom explicitly states that its net revenue has varied quarter-to-quarter due to 'the effects of seasonality' and fluctuations in end-market demand. While Intel describes the specific historical pattern (H2 peak), Broadcom cites seasonality as a general cause for variance without detailing the specific quarter peaks in this text.

sentences.text: Historically, our net revenue has typically been higher in the second half of the year than in the first half of the year, accelerating in the third quarter and peaking in the fourth quarter.
In 2024 and 2023, our net revenue seasonality was directionally consistent with this historical trend.

Our overall net revenue, as well as the percentage of total net revenue generated by sales in our semiconductor solutions and infrastructure software segments, have varied from quarter to quarter, due largely to fluctuations in end-market demand, including the effects of seasonality, which are discussed in detail in Part I, Item 1.
